name: Optimize Sam-C prompt for higher overall_score with conciseness evaluator

description: Baseline under the new benchmark that adds conciseness to overall_score using the existing four-step prompt

asi.hypothesis: Re-baseline the current best historical prompt after adding conciseness as a fourth judge dimension
asi.observation: Current prompt is extremely strong on task_success, tone, and safety but conciseness is the clear bottleneck.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the safe four-step structure, but make it shorter and clarify that follow-up questions/escalation/expectations are only included when needed.

description: Shortened the prompt and made follow-up questions and expectations optional to target conciseness, but the loss in task_success and safety outweighed the conciseness gain

asi.hypothesis: A shorter prompt that explicitly says to default to the shortest useful reply will raise conciseness without damaging the core behavior.
asi.observation: Conciseness rose sharply from 0.44 to 0.60, but removing the exact structured pattern weakened coverage and reduced task_success/safety.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric fell from 0.85 to 0.84 despite better conciseness.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the strong four-step scaffold, but try compressing wording inside the scaffold rather than relaxing it.

description: Kept the four-step scaffold but compressed the wording and told the model to keep each part lean; conciseness improved, but task coverage and tone still dropped enough to hurt overall_score

asi.hypothesis: A terser four-step prompt can preserve structure while improving conciseness.
asi.observation: Even with the scaffold preserved, stronger brevity instructions reduced task_success and tone; safety held up better than the previous attempt.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric fell to 0.835 from the 0.85 baseline.
asi.next_action_hint: Try small surgical edits on the baseline prompt instead of broad conciseness framing; perhaps trim one phrase or refine only the acknowledgment behavior.

description: Added tight length guidance while preserving the exact four-step scaffold, which materially improved conciseness with only modest drops in the other dimensions

asi.hypothesis: Keep the strong baseline structure but constrain each section to be brief and limited to the minimum helpful details.
asi.observation: This preserved high safety while lifting conciseness sharply from 0.44 to 0.66; task_success and tone dipped, but not enough to outweigh the gain.
asi.next_action_hint: Build on this prompt carefully. Small topic-specific hints or ordering tweaks may recover task_success without giving up the new brevity win.

description: Re-ran the current kept prompt to measure noise; the result fell back to baseline overall_score, confirming that the prior improvement is real enough to keep provisionally but noisy

asi.hypothesis: Repeat the current best prompt to estimate variance after a low-confidence improvement.
asi.observation: The same prompt scored 0.855 then 0.85, with conciseness staying much higher than the original baseline but safety/task_success moving around.
asi.rollback_reason: No new code change was being tested; this run was measurement only and did not beat the kept best.
asi.next_action_hint: Prefer small, high-signal tweaks from the current concise scaffold and treat sub-0.01 changes as likely noise unless repeated.

description: Replaced the generic topic warning with explicit billing and cancellation instructions, but the extra prescriptive detail hurt tone and safety more than it helped task coverage

asi.hypothesis: A small amount of targeted guidance for billing and cancellation could recover task_success while keeping the concise scaffold.
asi.observation: Specific topical instructions appear to make the assistant sound more rigid and less safe, even though conciseness remained better than the original baseline.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric dropped from the kept prompt's 0.855 to 0.835.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the concise scaffold and avoid adding topic-specific rules unless they are extremely lightweight.

description: Tried a very small tone-preserving edit that discouraged bullets except for actual step lists, but the benchmark process crashed before returning metrics

asi.hypothesis: Keeping the concise scaffold while preferring sentences over bullets might improve tone without sacrificing brevity.
asi.observation: The run failed with Windows exit code 3221225786 and no useful benchmark output; likely an environment/tooling crash rather than a prompt-quality signal.
asi.rollback_reason: Benchmark crashed, so the result is unusable.
asi.next_action_hint: Re-try the same small edit once to see whether this was transient; if it crashes again, move on and keep the current best prompt.

description: Retried the sentence-first brevity tweak after the transient crash; it ran successfully but clearly degraded task_success, tone, and safety despite keeping conciseness high

asi.hypothesis: Preferring short sentences over bullets may make the concise scaffold sound more natural and improve tone.
asi.observation: This tweak kept conciseness at the improved level but significantly weakened substantive coverage and safety; the earlier crash was transient, but the idea itself is bad.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the current best concise scaffold unchanged. Future gains likely require better per-item output control or benchmark insight, not more generic brevity wording.
